title: The factor-2 integrality-gap conjecture for the ATSP subtour LP
question: For every directed metric, is the minimum Hamiltonian-tour cost at most twice the optimum of the standard subtour-elimination linear program?
importance: Would identify the fundamental relaxation gap for asymmetric travelling salesman.
novelty_note: Distinct from the undirected 4/3 conjecture; these are the two classical TSP relaxation barriers.

title: Constant-factor approximation for Directed Feedback Vertex Set
question: Does a polynomial-time constant-factor approximation exist for minimum-weight directed feedback vertex set in arbitrary directed graphs?
importance: A defining approximation problem for directed cycle hitting.
novelty_note: TCS-6379 asks for a polynomial kernel, which is a different computational target; final search must also exclude another approximation record.

title: The Orthogonal Vectors Hypothesis
question: Is it true that for every epsilon>0 there is a constant c such that no randomized bounded-error word-RAM algorithm decides whether two n-element sets in {0,1}^{c log n} contain an orthogonal pair in O(n^{2-epsilon}) time?
importance: One of the central foundations for conditional lower bounds for strings, geometry and data structures.
novelty_note: TCS-6094 concerns restricted computational models; the proposed target is unrestricted word-RAM complexity.

title: The Hitting Set Conjecture
question: Is it true that for every epsilon>0 there is c such that deciding whether some a in A intersects every b in B, for two n-element families of subsets of [c log n], requires n^{2-o(1)} time against randomized bounded-error word-RAM algorithms?
importance: A standard hardness hypothesis behind fine-grained diameter and graph-distance barriers.
novelty_note: The existential-universal family problem, not the ordinary minimum hitting-set optimization problem.

title: Superpolynomial determinantal complexity of the permanent
question: Over characteristic zero, does representing the n by n permanent as the determinant of a matrix of affine-linear forms require superpolynomial matrix dimension?
importance: The classical determinant-versus-permanent barrier and a central target of geometric complexity theory.
novelty_note: TCS-5432 instead asks whether equivariant determinantal complexity is polynomially related to ordinary determinantal complexity; its full source was read.

title: Classical polynomial-time discrete logarithms in prime fields
question: Is there a randomized classical algorithm, polynomial in log p, that given a prime p, a generator g of F_p^*, and h in F_p^*, returns x with g^x=h?
importance: A central computational number-theory problem and a foundation of public-key cryptography.
novelty_note: The general prime-field algorithmic problem; not a specialized cryptanalytic attack.

title: Vinogradov's least quadratic nonresidue conjecture
question: For every epsilon>0, is the least positive quadratic nonresidue modulo an odd prime p bounded by p^epsilon for all sufficiently large p?
importance: A classical barrier in effective number theory governing the deterministic search for basic finite-field witnesses.
novelty_note: No matching question about least quadratic nonresidues was found; placement uses the computational number-theory scope.

title: A polynomial-time 2-approximation for Shortest Common Superstring
question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that always produces a common superstring of length at most twice optimum?
importance: The central unresolved approximation threshold for a fundamental sequence-assembly problem.
novelty_note: TCS-0816 primarily asks about exact exponential time and additionally mentions the stronger fixed-greedy-algorithm conjecture; TCS-1484 concerns MGREEDY and TCS-3843 multiplicities. Borderline overlap explicitly retained for editorial choice.

title: Constant-factor edit-distance approximation in near-linear time
question: Does some universal constant C admit a randomized bounded-error algorithm that C-approximates edit distance of two length-n strings in O(n polylog n) time?
importance: Would settle a main algorithmic frontier for the basic metric on strings.
novelty_note: TCS-4932's full source asks about a quantum advantage, not this classical target; near-linear-distance promises and n^{1+epsilon} algorithms do not settle the stated bound.

title: Fully dynamic minimum spanning forest with polylogarithmic worst-case updates
question: Can an exact minimum spanning forest of an undirected graph with polynomially bounded integer weights be maintained with polylogarithmic worst-case time per edge insertion or deletion and polynomial preprocessing and space?
importance: A longstanding worst-case barrier for one of the defining dynamic graph optimization problems.
novelty_note: TCS-0541 concerns low-stretch spanning trees, not minimum-weight spanning forests.

title: Fully dynamic near-optimal matching with polylogarithmic updates
question: For every fixed epsilon>0, can a (1+epsilon)-approximate maximum-cardinality matching be maintained in an arbitrary graph with polylogarithmic amortized update time, allowing randomization against an oblivious update sequence?
importance: The main approximation-versus-update-time barrier in dynamic matching.
novelty_note: TCS-0543 is about maximal matching; that is weaker than arbitrarily accurate maximum matching.

title: A deterministic FPTAS for the nonnegative permanent
question: Does a deterministic algorithm approximate the permanent of any nonnegative rational matrix within relative error epsilon in time polynomial in the input bit length and 1/epsilon?
importance: A landmark derandomization challenge for approximate counting.
novelty_note: Distinguish exact 2^n-time permanent computation from deterministic multiplicative approximation.

title: The optimal randomized metric distortion in social choice
question: Determine the infimum universal constant D for which an ordinal voting rule always selects a lottery whose expected total metric cost is at most D times the optimal candidate cost, over all numbers of voters and candidates and all consistent metrics.
importance: A defining limit on how much welfare can be recovered from ordinal preferences.
novelty_note: Use unrestricted randomized ordinal rules; the old conjecture D=2 is false, and tournament-only rules are a different restricted model.

title: Constant-factor truthful combinatorial auctions for submodular bidders
question: Does a universally truthful randomized mechanism using polynomial communication achieve a universal constant expected approximation to optimal welfare for arbitrary normalized monotone submodular valuations?
importance: The central question of whether incentive constraints destroy constant-factor welfare approximation in a standard multi-parameter auction model.
novelty_note: TCS-5229's selected source passage asks about a particular lower-bound construction; budget-feasible procurement is a different problem. Do not silently restrict to value queries.

title: Polynomial query complexity of exact envy-free cake cutting
question: Is there a deterministic Robertson-Webb protocol using polynomially many queries in n that completely allocates a cake envy-freely among n agents with arbitrary nonatomic additive valuations, allowing disconnected pieces?
importance: The principal complexity question behind exact envy-free division of a divisible resource.
novelty_note: TCS-1110 asks about mixed divisible/indivisible EFM; the 2025 paper gives an average-case bound under random valuations, not a worst-case polynomial protocol.

title: A complexity dichotomy for finite promise CSPs
question: For every fixed pair of finite relational templates A,B of the same signature with A mapping homomorphically to B, is the decision promise CSP distinguishing X->A from X not->B either in P or NP-hard?
importance: The main extension of the finite CSP classification theorem to promise problems.
novelty_note: TCS-1978 and TCS-1907 concern particular algorithmic subclasses; this is the full finite-template decision dichotomy.

title: The Bodirsky-Pinsker infinite-domain CSP dichotomy
question: Is CSP(B) always either in P or NP-complete when B is a finite-signature first-order reduct of a countable finitely bounded homogeneous relational structure?
importance: The principal tractability classification conjecture for well-behaved infinite-domain CSPs.
novelty_note: TCS-3203 asks about GSO definability and TCS-5924 a particular meta-question, rather than the full P/NP-complete dichotomy.

title: Constant-colour polynomial-time colouring of 3-colourable graphs
question: Is there a fixed integer C and a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs a proper C-colouring of every input graph promised to be 3-colourable?
importance: The paradigmatic unresolved approximate graph-colouring problem within promise CSP.
novelty_note: The constant C is existential and unrestricted; this is not the already-hard 3-to-4 or 3-to-5 problem.

title: Decidability of word equations with linear length constraints
question: Is satisfiability decidable for finite systems of word equations over a fixed finite alphabet combined with existential Presburger constraints on the lengths of their string variables?
importance: A fundamental decidability boundary for symbolic string reasoning and SMT string solvers.
novelty_note: TCS-6177 concerns equivalence of constrained pattern languages, which is a different quantified decision problem.

title: Decidability of termination for one-rule string rewriting
question: Given two words l,r, is it decidable whether the rewrite rule l->r admits no infinite rewriting sequence starting from any finite word?
importance: A minimal and longstanding unresolved termination problem in rewriting theory.
novelty_note: TCS-0874 asks about nontermination without loops; this target is decidability of uniform termination itself.

title: The conjugacy problem for one-relator groups
question: Is there an algorithm that, given a finite one-relator group presentation and two words, decides whether those words represent conjugate group elements?
importance: One of the classical Dehn decision problems in an exceptionally basic class of finitely presented groups.
novelty_note: TCS-0041 concerns embeddings of Baumslag-Solitar groups, and TCS-5506 inverse semigroups; neither is this conjugacy decision problem.

title: Martin's conjecture on degree-invariant functions
question: Under the usual determinacy assumptions, do Turing-invariant functions on reals obey Martin's full conjecture: the cone dichotomy below the identity and the well-ordering above it with jump as the successor operation?
importance: A proposed structural account of why the Turing jump governs natural computability-theoretic constructions.
novelty_note: No matching Martin-conjecture question was found. Results for order-preserving or uniformly invariant functions do not settle the general conjecture.

title: The reverse-mathematical strength of Hindman's theorem
question: Does Hindman's finite-sums theorem imply ACA_0^+ over RCA_0?
importance: The classical gap in the axiomatic strength of a central infinite combinatorial principle; this is a computability/logic question, not a new general-combinatorics category.
novelty_note: The theorem itself is known; the proposed target is equivalence with the established upper-bound system ACA_0^+.

title: Deterministic polynomial-time equivalence testing for d-DNNFs
question: Can one deterministically decide in polynomial time whether two given deterministic decomposable negation-normal-form Boolean circuits represent the same function?
importance: A basic unresolved operation in knowledge compilation, with consequences for checking and comparing compiled knowledge.
novelty_note: TCS-0306 is efficient complementation; equivalence testing is a separate fundamental operation.

title: Cereceda's quadratic recolouring conjecture
question: For every fixed d, does the reconfiguration graph of proper (d+2)-colourings of every n-vertex d-degenerate graph have diameter O_d(n^2), where one step recolours one vertex?
importance: The principal structural diameter conjecture in graph-colouring reconfiguration.
novelty_note: No matching Cereceda or general quadratic degenerate-recolouring question was found.

title: The planted-clique computational threshold
question: For every fixed epsilon in (0,1/2), is it impossible for a randomized polynomial-time algorithm to distinguish G(n,1/2) from G(n,1/2) with a uniformly planted clique of size floor(n^{1/2-epsilon}), with success probability at least 2/3?
importance: The foundational average-case hardness conjecture behind many proposed statistical-computational gaps.
novelty_note: TCS-1699/TCS-5257 use arbitrary base graphs, TCS-0422 a topological method, and TCS-5394 a low-degree model; the main unrestricted random-graph hypothesis is distinct.

title: The computational threshold for dense tensor PCA
question: For fixed tensor order k>=3, with a uniformly random unit spike v and iid standard Gaussian tensor noise Z, is polynomial-time weak recovery from lambda v^{tensor k}+Z impossible at lambda=n^{k/4-epsilon} for every fixed epsilon>0 in the statistically recoverable regime?
importance: A canonical separation between information-theoretic estimation and efficient algorithms in high-dimensional statistics.
novelty_note: No matching dense tensor-PCA threshold question was found; lower bounds for low-degree polynomials alone do not settle unrestricted polynomial-time recovery.
